note: Talks about the economics of marriage, making an argument that monogomy, fidelity, etc. are more functions of available resources for inheritence claims. In one example, with no farming land or other private wealth, some tribes expect to take care of children communally and without worry about paternal lineage. Another example considers farming land as non-fungible, with dividing the land reducing it to a lower from the sum than considering the whole (through efficiencies, say) and how this drives single son inheritence, which then drives increased dowry as the sons become the limited resource.
